what: decomposition of the pooled leave-one-positive-out AUROC of 0.3434 into the part attributable to pooling and the part attributable to the estimator, from C134b's stored fold statistics
targets_claim: Chapter 4 reports the gold-only nested cross-validation as '0.3434, AP 0.0362, one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 0.9666, worse than a constant-score floor' with no caveat

how_much_is_the_pooling.reading: both pooling-free estimates are below 0.3434, so the pooling flatters the estimator rather than depressing it; a reader who discounts 0.3434 as a pooling artifact is discounting it in the wrong direction

per_stratum.stratum: non-degenerate out-of-fold score span, at or above 0.001
wide out-of-fold score span, at or above 0.01

spearman_fold_score_span_vs_fold_auroc.caveat: 12 folds, each AUROC on a 1/20 or 1/21 grid, folds not independent; read as descriptive

how_much_is_a_degenerate_estimator.reading: the degenerate folds sit NEARER chance than the folds with real score spread, so the below-chance result is not the degenerate folds' rounding error; it is concentrated in the folds where the fitted model does separate rows

which_caveat_is_true.verdict: neither as stated. Pooling flatters the number, and the near-constant folds are the ones nearest chance. What the estimator shows is a consistent below-chance ranking that survives both pooling-free estimates and is strongest where the fitted model is least degenerate.

sentence_the_thesis_should_carry: That pooled figure is not the only estimate available, and it is the most favourable one: the mean of the 12 per-fold AUROCs is 0.2667 and pooling within-fold mid-ranks instead of raw probabilities gives 0.2656, so the pooling raises the figure rather than depressing it. Half the folds fit a near-constant model, with an out-of-fold score span below 0.001 over their 20 or 21 negatives, but those folds average 0.3833 and the folds with real score spread average 0.1500, so the below-chance ranking is not those folds' rounding error. At 12 positives and one positive per fold the estimate is too coarse to support a claim of inverse discrimination; what it does not support is any claim of discrimination.
